threads.body: `rm "$fragment"` can treat a path beginning with `-` as an option (quotes don’t prevent that), which is risky for file deletion. Use `rm -- "$fragment"` (and consider `-f` if the script runs with `set -e`) to make deletion robust and non-option-injectable.

+# remove any changelog fragments on main that were included in this release section
+changelog_dir="$(dirname "${CHANGELOG}")/.changelog"

+    for fragment in "$changelog_dir"/*; do
+        if [[ -f "$fragment" ]]; then
+            frag_name=$(basename "$fragment")
+            if [[ "$frag_name" != .* ]]; then
+                pr_num="${frag_name%%.*}"
+                if grep -q "\[#${pr_num}\]" /tmp/CHANGELOG_SECTION.md; then
+                    rm "$fragment"

threads.body: This `grep` pattern is regex-based; while `pr_num` is likely numeric, using fixed-string matching avoids accidental regex interpretation and makes intent clearer. Consider switching to `grep -Fq "[#${pr_num}]" /tmp/CHANGELOG_SECTION.md` for a literal match.
